draft.title: Globalisation and technologies
card: the growing links between societies through trade, media, travel and the movement of ideas. Events and choices in one place can affect people far away.
the tools and methods people use to do tasks. They can change how people live, work and communicate.
Technologies such as the internet and cheap air travel make globalisation faster. People can share music, news and ideas across the world in seconds.
These links can change a culture, for example by bringing in new foods, languages or ways of working. A society may also keep or adapt its own customs.
draft.remember: Globalisation links societies. Technologies change daily life and can speed up those links.

opts: A Korean TV series is watched by teenagers in Australia
A school in Bathurst buys a new set of laptops
A family in Perth builds a new backyard shed
A town council in Wagga repaints its public library
a.why: Teenagers in Australia watching a Korean series shows media linking two societies. The laptops are a technology, but buying them does not link societies by itself.
a.clue: Look for a link between societies in different places.

b.q: Priya lives in Sydney and works from home for a company in Germany. She talks with her team by video each day. What does this best show?
opts: Technologies helping globalisation link two societies
Globalisation causing a technology to be invented
A culture refusing to change over time
A society ending all trade with other societies
b.why: Video calls are a technology, and they let Priya work with people in another society, which is a link of globalisation. The other option about invention reverses cause and effect: nothing in the case says globalisation created the technology.
b.clue: Name the technology first, then the link it makes.

a.best: A Korean TV series is watched by teenagers in Australia

b.best: Technologies helping globalisation link two societies
